text:
Short answer: Not automatically. The manual shows that “Signal Lost behavior” is configurable and can be set to Return to Home, Hover, or Land. So the EVO Max 4N will return home after losing the link only if the operator has selected Return to Home as the Signal Lost action.

text: FAA guidance indicates reestablishing the control link after a lost-link hazard and discontinuing flight or avoiding further operations until testing the control link. The Autel EVO Max 4N manual states RTH is triggered when Return to Home is active or Auto RTH is selected. It also says the drone will continue flying until the disconnection message appears, and that a link restoration within 10 seconds will automatically return control to the remote. Incident reports (unverified) claim the UAS lost control shortly after takeoff and that Return To Home failed. Gaps and conflicts: it is unclear whether RTH was engaged in the incident, whether the 10-second auto-return applied, and how model-specific Autel behavior reconciles with FAA guidance.
